source_title: CMS Emergency room rights under EMTALA
locator: “Give you an appropriate medical screening exam”; insurance inquiry must not delay exam/treatment; uninsured patients still offered screening.
source_setting: US hospital emergency-care context described by CMS
quantity: Insurance inquiry cannot delay emergency care
value: Insurance questions may be asked only without delaying examination or treatment; screening is offered even without insurance.
source_evidence_basis: CMS EMTALA rights page states that a hospital may ask about insurance at check-in only if doing so does not delay the medical screening exam or treatment, and must offer screening even to uninsured patients.
limitations: This is a plain-language CMS summary of EMTALA protections, not a complete legal analysis or benefit/payment determination. Applies to emergency departments within EMTALA scope.
inferred_scenario_use: Do not place insurance authorization as a gate before emergency screening/stabilization in the simulation; allow parallel administrative work.

source_title: The effect of discharge destination and primary insurance provider on hospital discharge delays among patients with traumatic brain injury: a multicenter study of 1,543 patients
locator: Abstract, Methods/Results; Results, Discharge delays; Table 1. Discharge delay defined as discharge >=24 hours after case-management documentation that patient was ready.
source_setting: Four Level I trauma centers in three US states; adults with TBI and Injury Severity Score >=9.
source_n: 1,543 patients total; 210 (13.6%, rounded in abstract to 14%) experienced discharge delay. Reason counts use 210 delayed patients as denominator and can overlap.
quantity: Reported delay reasons among delayed patients
unit: percent of patients with discharge delay; overlapping reasons
source_evidence_basis: Retrospective multicenter patient cohort with medical-record abstraction. Table 1 gives insurance authorization 109/210 (51.9%, rounded in abstract to 52%), no accepting bed 85/210 (40.5%, rounded to 41%), patient-related reasons 72/210 (34.3%, rounded to 34%). Reasons overlap.
limitations: Restricted to adult moderate/severe TBI at four trauma centers and delays >=24 hours after documented readiness. Reason assignment is record-based and overlapping; it is not a PA response-time measure or a general all-hospital rate. Not RWJ data.
inferred_scenario_use: Represent post-acute placement authorization separately from acceptance/bed availability after clinical readiness. Use the 52% as a contextual blocker category among delayed TBI cases only, not as an individual probability or PA duration.
